newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Nelson Mandela announced on Wednesday that South Africa would cut formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan, recognising China instead.
- Life group Metropolitan Life Ltd posted a 26 percent rise in attributable surplus to 134 million rand in the year to September, buoyed by robust growth in premium and investment income.
- The rand hit its best level against the dollar in more than five weeks on Wednesday as demand rose when offshore banks developed a healthy appetite for South African bonds.

- Glitches in the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's updated screen trading system, Jet II, have cost the exchange at least 400 million rand in turnover in the past three days, forcing it to revert to the original version introduced nine months ago.
- The rand gained more than three cents on Wednesday to finish below 4.59 against the dollar for the second consecutive day.

- Metlife, the life insurance company controlled by New Africa Investments Ltd, posted a 26 percent increase in attributable income to 134 million rand in the year to September 30 because of strong gains in premium and investment income.

- Analysts expressed concern on Wednesday about the size of the premium that African Mining Group has agreed to pay Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd for a 34.9 percent stake in mining house JCI Ltd.
- Unrelenting problems with the electronic trading system, or Jet, brought the Johannesburg Stock Exchange to a halt for the third consecutive day on Wednesday.
- South Africa is to break off diplomatic ties with Taiwan in favour of mainland China, President Nelson Mandela announced on Wednesday.
